question.problem: Find a unit normal vector to the level curve of the function $f(x,y)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)-xy$ that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(2,-1).$
question.worked_solution:
A normal vector to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(2,-1)$, can be found by computing $∇f(2,-1).$ 

So, we first find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(2,-1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)-xy)\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)-xy)\text{ }j \\  & =(\frac{1}{x+y}-y)\text{ }i+(\frac{1}{x+y}-x)\text{ }j \\ ∇f(2,-1) & =(\frac{1}{2+(-1)}-(-1))\text{ }i+(\frac{1}{2+(-1)}-2)\text{ }j \\  & =2i-j\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize $∇f(2,-1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∇f(2,-1)}{‖∇f(2,-1)‖} & =\frac{2i-j}{\sqrt{{(2)}^{2}+{(-1)}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{2i-j}{\sqrt{5}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{5}(2i-j)\end{aligned}
$$
